class.name: NNSTRoot
class.brief_description: The root node for a State Tree.
class.description: This is the root node for a State Tree. The root ticks itself: while it is in the scene tree and enabled, the SceneTree's [code]process_frame[/code] or [code]physics_frame[/code] signal selected by [member process_thread] calls [method tick], which updates the child sensors and lets every active state run its [method NNSTTickedNodes.on_tick] method from the root down to the leaf. Automatic ticking is on by default. The root does not override or disable this node's own [code]_process[/code]/[code]_physics_process[/code], so a script attached to the root keeps its own callbacks and cannot shadow automatic ticking. Connections exist only while the root is in the tree with [member is_enabled] true and a [member process_thread] other than [constant MANUAL], and no tick happens while the root cannot process (paused or process mode disabled). [constant MANUAL] connects neither signal, so a custom scheduler calls [method tick] or [method auto_tick_step] itself. An inactive chart is never ticked automatically. A root that was transitioned out stays dormant until its owner re-enters it, because [method tick] on a root with no active states transitions the chart in again; its owner decides when that should happen. A root placed in a scene becomes active on [constant NOTIFICATION_READY], so the normal flow ticks from the first frame. Call [method tick] directly to re-enter an inactive root by hand. [member tick_rate] counts eligible frame signal emissions, starting with the first one. A rate of 2 ticks on emissions 1, 3, 5 and so on. The schedule counts emissions, not time, but each tick receives the delta accumulated since the previous tick. Re-arming the schedule (changing [member tick_rate], [member process_thread] or [member is_enabled], and entering or leaving the tree) restarts the count and discards any accumulated delta, so the next eligible emission is due. The root can be hosted. A host is an ancestor state ([NNSTTickedNodes]) that is active or an ancestor agent action ([NNAction]) that is the agent's current action, and the nearest host ancestor is the one that drives the root. A root nested inside another root's subtree is not hosted across that root; the nearest ancestor root owns its subtree. A host starts the chart when it activates and ticks it with the host's own delta on the host's schedule, so a hosted root never ticks from the SceneTree frame signals and never enters the chart on [constant NOTIFICATION_READY]: the first host tick transitions it in. The host owns the timing, so the root's [member process_thread] and [member tick_rate] are ignored and the editor shows a configuration warning when either would be. Deactivating the host exits the active states and leaves the root inactive, so a later activation starts a fresh chart. Events sent with [method send_event] are queued and processed one at a time in FIFO order. The root is the last state to see an event: the event is delivered to the innermost active state first and bubbles up to its ancestors until a state consumes it. Only when no active child consumed the event are transitions attached directly to the root tried. A transition attached directly to the root can only leave the root's current active child: when its target is the child that is already active, the transition does nothing. Re-entering a state directly is not supported either, because [method NNSTTickedNodes.transition_to] rejects a transition whose source and target are the same state. Transition to a different state first and then back to re-enter a state. The root also owns the change pipeline used by automatic transitions. Pending state changes and property changes are processed before queued events, under a reentrancy lock, so a transition caused by a change is fully applied before the next change is handled. [member blackboard] is the explicitly assigned [NNBlackboard], and an explicit assignment always wins. When it is null the root inherits the effective board of the nearest ancestor root of any Noodle Nodes system, and falls back to its own private per-instance board only when it has no root ancestor. The private board is never a property, so it is never serialised. [member actor] is the explicitly assigned actor; read the resolved actor with [method get_actor], which resolves the live explicit actor, then [member actor_node_path], then the actor of the nearest ancestor root, then the root's parent. Both are resolved from the root's current position in the scene tree on demand, so reparenting re-resolves them, and a freed explicit actor falls through to the path, the inherited actor or the parent.

constants.constant: The root is ticked automatically from the SceneTree's [code]process_frame[/code] signal.
The root is ticked automatically from the SceneTree's [code]physics_frame[/code] signal. This is the default.
Neither signal is connected and the root never ticks automatically, so a custom scheduler calls [method tick] or [method auto_tick_step] itself.
No trigger type. Used as a default value.
The transition is triggered by an event sent with [method send_event].
The transition is automatic and is triggered when its state is entered. Supported by every automatic transition.
The transition is automatic and is triggered by a change to an expression property. Reported by [NNSTExpressionGuard].
The transition is automatic and is triggered by a change of which states are active. Reported by [NNSTStateIsActiveGuard].

method.name: auto_tick_step
method.description: The shared body of the frame-signal handlers, and the deterministic driver for custom schedulers. Ticks the chart when the call is due, and returns [code]true[/code] only when it actually ticked. The tick receives the [param delta] plus the deltas of the non-due calls since the previous tick, so states measure the elapsed time rather than one frame's worth. The call is ignored, returning [code]false[/code], when [param process_thread] is not the selected [member process_thread], when the selected thread is [constant MANUAL], when the root is disabled, in the editor, when the chart is inactive (see [method get_is_active]), or when [member tick_rate] makes this invocation not due. An ignored call does not advance the [member tick_rate] schedule. This method also works outside the tree, so tests and custom schedulers can drive the schedule deterministically without frame signals.

method.name: get_child_sensors
method.description: Returns a list of child sensors.

method.name: send_event
method.description: Queues an event for processing and emits [signal event_received]. Events are processed in FIFO order, one at a time. Calling this method from a callback (for example [method NNSTTickedNodes.on_enter_state], [method NNSTTickedNodes.on_exit_state] or a guard) queues the event instead of processing it recursively. The event is handled only after the transition that is running and all of its callbacks have completed, whether that transition came from an event or from a direct [method NNSTTickedNodes.transition_to] call. Each event is delivered to the innermost active state first and then bubbles up through its ancestors until a state consumes it, so a compound state only handles the event when its active child did not. Transitions attached directly to the root are tried last; a root-level transition whose target is the currently active root child does nothing. A processing pass that applies more than 100 transitions is treated as an infinite loop: an error is printed, the pending queue is discarded, the chart is marked invalid and later events are ignored.

method.name: tick
method.description: Updates the State Tree. When no states are active the chart is transitioned in, then the child sensors are evaluated and every active state's [method NNSTTickedNodes.on_tick] method is called from the root down to the leaf with [param delta]. The tree reads and writes its data through the effective [NNBlackboard], which any state reaches with [method NoodleNodes.get_blackboard] and the other blackboard helpers. The resolved actor is available to every state as [method NoodleNodes.get_actor]. This is the manual entry point: automatic ticking calls it too. Calling it is the only way to re-enter an inactive chart by hand, so with [member process_thread] set to [constant MANUAL] a custom scheduler can own the timing.

method.name: get_assigned_blackboard
method.description: Returns the explicitly assigned blackboard, or [code]null[/code] when none is assigned. This is the value of [member blackboard]. Use [method NoodleNodes.get_blackboard_resource] to read the effective board, which is the assigned board, the board inherited from the nearest ancestor root, or this root's private board.

method.name: set_blackboard_resource
method.description: Assigns [param blackboard] as the root's blackboard. An explicit assignment wins over the board inherited from an ancestor root. Assigning [code]null[/code] clears the assignment and returns to inherited resolution, which is the nearest ancestor root's board or this root's private board.

method.name: get_assigned_actor
method.description: Returns the explicitly assigned actor, or [code]null[/code] when none is assigned or the assigned actor was freed. This is the value of [member actor]. Use [method get_actor] to read the resolved actor, which may be inherited from an ancestor root or fall back to the root's parent.

method.name: set_actor
method.description: Assigns [param actor] as the root's explicit actor. Assigning [code]null[/code] clears the assignment, so resolution returns to [member actor_node_path], then the nearest ancestor root's actor, then the root's parent.

method.name: set_actor_node_path
method.description: Sets the fallback actor path, resolved relative to this root. It is used when no live explicit [member actor] is set and wins over the actor inherited from an ancestor root.

method.name: get_actor_node_path
method.description: Returns the fallback actor path. This is the value of [member actor_node_path].

method.name: set_expression_property
method.description: Sets a property that expression guards can reference by name (for example [code]flag[/code] can be used as [code]flag == true[/code] in an expression). The value is stored in [member blackboard]. Setting the property marks a property change pending and re-evaluates automatic transitions that support [constant PROPERTY_CHANGE].

method.name: get_expression_property
method.description: Returns the value of a previously set expression property, or [param default] when it has not been set. Expression property values are stored in [member blackboard] under the property name.

members.member: The explicitly assigned actor, or [code]null[/code] when none is assigned. No resolved fallback is ever stored here. To read the resolved actor use [method get_actor], which resolves the explicit actor, then [member actor_node_path], then the actor of the nearest ancestor root of any Noodle Nodes system, then the root's parent on demand.
Fallback actor path, used when no live explicit [member actor] is set. The path is resolved relative to this root and wins over the actor inherited from an ancestor root.

The explicitly assigned typed state tree blackboard resource, or [code]null[/code] when none is assigned. An explicit assignment always wins. When it is [code]null[/code] the root inherits the effective board of the nearest ancestor root of any Noodle Nodes system and uses its own private per-instance board only when it has no root ancestor, so the blackboard helpers work without any setup. Assigning [code]null[/code] clears the assignment and returns to inherited resolution. The private board is never a property, so it is never serialised. Blackboards default to [code]resource_local_to_scene = true[/code], so an assigned inspector board is per scene instance unless you deliberately untick it to share one board. This property is the assignment only; [method NoodleNodes.get_blackboard_resource] returns the effective board. Expression properties are stored in this board as well.

Initial values for expression properties. They are written into [member blackboard] when the root first transitions in, before any state is entered, so expressions are always valid on the first evaluation.

Selects the SceneTree frame signal that drives automatic ticking, not this node's processing flags. Defaults to [constant PHYSICS], so a root auto-ticks once added to a scene. [constant IDLE] uses [code]process_frame[/code], [constant PHYSICS] uses [code]physics_frame[/code] and [constant MANUAL] connects neither so a custom scheduler ticks the chart. Exactly one signal is connected at a time. Out-of-range values fall back to [constant PHYSICS]. Setting this property re-arms the [member tick_rate] schedule. Ignored while an ancestor state or agent action hosts the root, because the host drives every tick; the editor reports a configuration warning when the value would be ignored.

The number of eligible frame signal emissions between automatic ticks. The default of [code]1[/code] ticks every eligible emission, and a rate of 2 ticks on emissions 1, 3, 5 and so on. Values below 1 are clamped to 1. Ineligible emissions, such as those for a signal that is not selected, do not advance the count. A tick receives the delta accumulated over the emissions since the previous tick, so the states measure the same elapsed time whatever the rate. Setting this property or [member process_thread], an [member is_enabled] change, and entering or leaving the tree re-arm the schedule and discard the accumulated delta. The rate gates the whole tick, including running actions, so it stays at [code]1[/code] by default; [NNAgent] defaults to [code]6[/code] because its rate only throttles thinking. Ignored while an ancestor state or agent action hosts the root, and the editor reports a configuration warning when the value would be ignored.
The time to complete a tick in usec.

signal.name: event_received
signal.description: Emitted once for each event processed by this root, before the event is delivered to the active states. See [method send_event].

signal.name: finished
signal.description: Emitted with [param succeeded] set to [code]true[/code] when a state with [member NNSTTickedNodes.is_final] is entered, which reports the chart as finished. Final states do not stop ticking by themselves; the chart keeps running until a host deactivates it or it is transitioned out.
